title: Digital Dilemmas & Online Respect
subject: PSHE / Computing · KS2
objective: I can explain why we ask permission before sharing online, tell respectful from disrespectful behaviour, and know how to support a friend online.

slides.title: Digital Hero Academy
slides.sub: I can explain why we ask permission before sharing online, tell respectful from disrespectful behaviour, and know how to support a friend online.

slides.title: What makes showing respect online different from offline?
slides.hint: Think about what you can’t see or hear when you’re behind a screen.

slides.title: Respectful or disrespectful?
slides.hint: Tap a word, then tap where it belongs.

slides.title: Finish the sentence: “Respect means…”
slides.hint: When everyone’s answers are shown, tap ❤️ on the best sentence. We’ll choose one as a class.

slides.title: How easy is it to pause and think before pressing send?
How does David feel? How could his friend fix this right now?
Is it ever OK to post a picture of a friend without asking?
options: Only if it’s a nice photo
Yes, if they’re my best friend
slides.hint: What if your parents post photos of you? How is sharing a photo like lending something you own?

slides.title: Amrit said no, but gave in. Who is responsible for the nasty posts?
Which golden rule is hardest to follow online?
slides.hint: Put the hardest at the top.

slides.title: What should Lisa do?
slides.hint: Which digital tool from the last slide could she use?

slides.title: Case files: solve the dilemma
slides.hint: Use your Respect Radar, Consent Padlock and Support Flowchart.

cases.name: Reena’s case
cases.text: Reena left a group chat because it had turned nasty. A friend messaged her a link to a horrible video from the chat anyway.

cases.name: Anthony’s case
cases.text: Anthony thinks his friend has made new friends. When his friend leaves his phone unlocked, Anthony looks through his messages.

cases.name: Sarah’s case
cases.text: Sarah keeps her profile very private and uses a secret nickname. Someone she trusted gave her nickname away to a person at school.

cases.name: Amrit’s case
cases.text: Amrit’s friend kept pestering him for his login, so he gave in. The friend then posted nasty messages from Amrit’s account.

cases.name: David’s case
cases.text: David asked not to be in the trip photos because his parents don’t let him use social media. A friend secretly took photos of him and posted them.

cases.name: Lisa’s case
cases.text: Lisa sees a group of gamers being horrible to one player. She doesn’t want to feel left out, so she joins in and sends a mean message too.

slides.title: Is it OK to give your password to your best friend if they promise not to misuse it?
options: Yes, if they’re your best friend
slides.explain: Your password is the key to your digital identity. You are responsible for anything posted from your account.

slides.title: What word means stepping in to help when something unfair is happening?
slides.explain: To intervene is to step in safely, or to get help from a trusted adult.

slides.title: What must you do before uploading a photo from a group trip?
options: Ask everyone in it for permission
slides.explain: Photo consent isn’t optional. Everyone in the picture gets a say.

slides.title: A friend is upset by comments in a group chat. What is the best thing to do first?
options: Tell them to just ignore it
Listen, and help them report it
slides.explain: Listen first, then help them report or block, and tell a trusted adult if it carries on.

slides.title: Why use a nickname and private account settings?
options: To control who can find and contact you
So you can be unkind without anyone knowing
slides.explain: Private settings and nicknames help you decide who can find you and contact you.

slides.title: Recipe for a perfect online friend: what are the key ingredients?
slides.hint: Up to 3 words or short phrases, e.g. kindness, listening, asking permission.

slides.title: Draw your perfect online friend.
slides.hint: What do they know? How do they treat people? What tools do they use?

slides.title: Your Digital Hero Toolkit is complete
How confident are you?
